title: News-Driven Return Reversals: Liquidity Provision Ahead of Earnings Announcements
one_line: Short-term reversals are six times larger around earnings announcements (3-day loser-minus-winner 1.45% vs 0.22% otherwise, 1996-2011) as market makers demand more compensation ahead of the news.

findings.statement: Six-fold increase in reversals around announcements; 1.45% vs 0.22% (3 days).
Large-stock strategy ~6.5%/yr, Sharpe 1.73 before costs; slightly negative out of sample (Quantpedia).

why.pattern: Liquidity provision / inventory risk before scheduled news.

reported_results.headline: Short-term reversals are six times larger around earnings announcements (3-day loser-minus-winner 1.45% vs 0.22% otherwise, 1996-2011) as market makers demand more compensation ahead of the news.

data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
